title: Liquidity and credit without run-prone debt

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a national financial architecture that supplies reliable everyday payments while funding risky loans without private promises that investors can demand back immediately at a fixed value. It would separate the money households and businesses use for payments from the credit risk of lending, while preserving the assessment of borrowers, monitoring of loans and supply of credit.

One proposed route combines payment claims fully backed by a specified public settlement instrument with lending financed by equity or other funding that cannot trigger an immediate fixed-value redemption obligation. Equity illustrates the mechanism: investors can sell their shares, potentially at a loss, but cannot require the issuer to redeem them on demand and thereby force liquidation. The broader concept does not require every lender to use equity exclusively; it requires the funding arrangements to avoid recreating runnable promises elsewhere in the system.

This is a proposed institutional capability, distinct from explaining how existing banks create money. Commercial-bank lending already creates matching deposits under the arrangements described by the Bank of England. Understanding that process does not itself establish an architecture that preserves payment liquidity and lending while removing runnable private funding.

significance.text: Instantly accessible, fixed-value deposits can fund assets that repay over months or years. If depositors seek repayment together, a bank may be unable to meet those demands without selling assets or obtaining emergency funding. An architecture that maintained payments and adequate credit while eliminating this funding mechanism would remove a major route through which investment losses become disruptive runs. Its revolutionary contribution would be dependable financial services despite losses on risky investments.

Deposit guarantees and emergency public liquidity can counter runs while retaining contingent public exposure; their use does not necessarily produce taxpayer losses. Under the proposed architecture, investment losses would instead fall on the designated private risk bearers without giving them a contractual route to force immediate repayment from the payment system. Those risk bearers could include equity investors and holders of suitable non-runnable debt.

Conditional synthesis: if this separation worked at national scale without impairing underwriting or credit supply, it could reduce the need for emergency protection of private funding and make losses easier to resolve without interrupting essential payments. These benefits depend on effective implementation and on preventing runnable substitutes from emerging outside the regulated perimeter.

Removing contractual funding runs would not eliminate every financial panic, recession or payment interruption. Asset prices could still fall sharply, borrowers could default, sovereign obligations could become risky and payment infrastructure could fail operationally. A decline in an equity-financed lender's share price is also different from a redemption run: it imposes a market loss without necessarily creating an immediate repayment obligation for the lender. The claimed advance concerns a particular destabilizing mechanism, rather than universal financial stability.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central economic challenge is to preserve the useful functions that fragile funding may perform while eliminating its run mechanism. Cochrane's discussion attributes to Diamond and Rajan a mechanism in which short-term investors monitor and discipline intermediaries, supporting lending against otherwise illiquid assets. If such discipline materially enables credit, replacing deposits with safer contracts must also replace that function. Cochrane questions the mechanism's quantitative importance, so this is a model-dependent challenge rather than an established universal requirement that banks must be fragile. The supplied review could not directly verify Diamond and Rajan's precise argument or assumptions because neither their working paper nor journal text was available for inspection.

A workable design must jointly provide accessible payment balances, effective borrower screening and monitoring, and financing for assets that cannot be liquidated quickly at predictable prices. Merely changing the legal name of a deposit or raising a bank's capital ratio does not establish that these functions survive without runnable funding. The unresolved capability is their reliable combination across an economy, including during stress.

Engineering synthesis: implementation would require enforceable backing and redemption rules, a payment infrastructure that continues operating when lenders fail, and insolvency arrangements that allocate investment losses without freezing essential transactions. Regulation would need to cover economically equivalent promises in shadow banking as well as conventional banks. Transition arrangements would also need to preserve viable lending while existing funding contracts change. These are design requirements inferred from the target capability, not demonstrated solutions in the supplied record.

current_state.text: Michael McLeay, Amar Radia and Ryland Thomas's Bank of England Quarterly Bulletin article, published on 14 March 2014 in the 2014 Q1 issue, explains that most money in the modern economy is created through commercial-bank lending. It rejects accounts in which banks simply lend out previously deposited savings or mechanically multiply central-bank money. The supplied review had a complete 14-page PDF extraction as well as the article landing page. This establishes an available descriptive account of money creation, not a demonstration of run-free credit provision.

John H. Cochrane's essay dated 16 April 2014, Toward a Run-Free Financial System, proposes eliminating runnable private securities while retaining financial services and credit. It argues that modern financial, computational and communication technology addresses longstanding practical objections to narrow banking. The supplied review verified the essay's identity and relevant passages, including its discussion of monitoring incentives and credit continuity. Its retained extraction ends on page 43, so these conclusions rest on the available portions. The essay documents an argued reform design, not an economy-wide implementation.

The research identifies Douglas W. Diamond and Raghuram G. Rajan's Liquidity Risk, Liquidity Creation and Financial Fragility: A Theory of Banking as a December 1999 working paper subsequently published in the Journal of Political Economy in 2001. However, no inspectable copy of either version was supplied to the review. The earlier wording that fragile capital structure is necessary therefore cannot be retained as a directly verified, unrestricted conclusion. Cochrane's secondary discussion supports the existence of a theoretical tradeoff, while leaving the original model's exact assumptions and scope unresolved.

The Federal Reserve's review dated 28 April 2023 documents that Silicon Valley Bank lost more than $40 billion in deposits on 9 March 2023 and was closed on 10 March. This is a concrete example of a rapid funding run within the existing banking system. The supplied review verified these facts in the executive summary and verified the report date in its PDF. The executive summary is only part of the report; the retained PDF extraction was truncated and some pages lacked extractable text. Those limitations do not prevent verification of the stated dates and withdrawal amount, but the episode alone does not establish global nonadoption of alternative architectures.

The supplied research lists Stephen Williamson's Deposit insurance, bank regulation, and narrow banking as a July 2024 Journal of Economic Theory article, volume 219, article 105859, and reports DOI 10.1016/j.jet.2024.105859. It attributes to the model a conclusion that narrow banking is never welfare-improving and that its viability depends on inefficient regulation of conventional banks. No saved text was available to the review, so the identity, bibliographic correction and reported conclusions remain unverified here. Even if confirmed, the result would concern the model's assumptions and welfare comparison, rather than establish that every possible architecture must fail.

Evidence-limited synthesis: the supplied materials establish a descriptive account of bank money creation, a documented reform proposal and a subsequent major bank run. They do not establish that the proposed national capability has been achieved, nor do they establish its worldwide absence as of 1 November 2026. The supplied freshness search record is empty, leaving present adoption and demonstration status unresolved.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: a national retail payment and credit system would operate for a pre-registered multiyear period without demandable, fixed-value private debt except payment claims fully backed by a specified public settlement instrument. The protocol would define the backing assets, enforceable redemption rights, treatment of encumbrances and system perimeter, including economically equivalent funding outside conventional banks. These are proposed criteria for this architecture, not established standards.
completion_criteria.label: Multiyear operation restricts runnable private debt to fully publicly-backed payment claims

completion_criteria.text: A pre-specified qualifying stress episode would then test whether the system avoids a funding run and interruption of essential payments without a taxpayer guarantee of private investment losses. The evaluation would distinguish private loss absorption from public settlement services and record the terms and recipients of any emergency support. A higher capital ratio in an otherwise runnable system, or a paper design without operation, would not satisfy this proposed demonstration.
completion_criteria.label: Stress preserves payments without funding runs or taxpayer-guaranteed investment losses

completion_criteria.text: Credit to households and nonfinancial firms would need to avoid a large, sustained contraction relative to a pre-registered counterfactual. Before testing, evaluators would specify stress severity, credit measures, contraction thresholds and duration, and how they would distinguish weak loan demand from impaired credit supply. They would also assess underwriting, borrower monitoring and information production, so that continued lending volumes alone could not conceal a deterioration in lending quality.
completion_criteria.label: Credit avoids large sustained contraction while preserving lending quality

completion_criteria.text: Independent evaluators should be able to reproduce the findings from documented contracts, balance sheets, payment records, credit data and the specified counterfactual method, subject to appropriate access protections. Repeated stress tests and operational experience across differing economic conditions would strengthen the case. A finite demonstration would establish performance within observed conditions and stated boundaries; it would not prove immunity to every future run mechanism, sovereign shock or operational failure.
completion_criteria.label: Independent evaluators reproduce findings within observed conditions and stated boundaries

related_concepts.text: Narrow banking, public money, equity-funded lending and shadow-banking reform overlap directly with ECO-10. Narrow banking addresses the backing of payment claims; public money supplies a possible settlement instrument; equity and other non-runnable funding allocate investment risk; and shadow-banking reform addresses substitutes that could recreate runs elsewhere. ECO-10 combines these concerns into the broader requirement that reliable payments coexist with effective lending across the national system.

Roster-based synthesis: ECO-06, Household-scale markets for national, occupational, and housing income risk, concerns transferring household income risks. ECO-10 concerns the funding contracts and payment arrangements through which financial institutions operate. A run-resistant architecture could support risk-sharing markets, but it would not itself create those markets. ECO-05, Approximately efficient voluntary provision of global public goods, overlaps through financial stability's collective benefits, while addressing a different problem of voluntary contribution and provision.

Roster-based synthesis: ECO-08, Structural counterfactuals for macroeconomic regimes, could help evaluate how credit and welfare would differ under a changed banking regime; ECO-02, Prospective transport of causal policy effects across populations, concerns whether evidence from one jurisdiction or trial applies elsewhere. Both matter to assessing ECO-10, but credible evaluation methods are distinct from constructing the financial architecture. ECO-01, Empirically valid aggregate market laws beyond the Sonnenschein–Mantel–Debreu barrier, seeks general aggregate regularities; ECO-10 targets a specific institutional mechanism.

Roster-based synthesis: ECO-03, A predictive and welfare-coherent theory of boundedly rational choice, could inform analysis of depositor and investor behavior, but removing runnable contracts is a separate design objective. ECO-04, An interpersonally comparable, preference-respecting measure of welfare, concerns how benefits and losses across people should be compared. ECO-10 can propose operational tests for payment continuity and credit preservation without claiming to solve that welfare-measurement problem.

Roster-based synthesis: ECO-09, A general, detail-free allocation compiler for private-information economies, overlaps with the challenge of preserving borrower screening, monitoring and incentives, but seeks a much more general allocation capability. ECO-07, A verified, manipulable law of sustained productivity growth, concerns sustained productivity rather than funding stability. Better financial continuity might support productive investment, but achieving ECO-10 would establish neither such a growth law nor a guaranteed productivity gain. Forecasting credit distress is also a separate task; the supplied material does not establish its comparative degree of achievement.

change_log.change: Preserved ECO-10's identity and expanded the explanation of payment backing, private risk bearing and non-runnable lending finance.
change_log.reason: The research and review jointly describe a substantive institutional capability whose functions should remain clear independently of disputed supporting claims.

change_log.change: Replaced the unrestricted Diamond–Rajan necessity claim with a model-dependent monitoring and discipline challenge, including Cochrane's disagreement about quantitative importance.
change_log.reason: The review had secondary evidence but no inspectable Diamond–Rajan text to verify the original quotation, assumptions or universal scope.

change_log.change: Narrowed the claimed impact from eliminating financial panic generally to eliminating a major contractual funding-run mechanism.
change_log.reason: Asset-price panics, recessions, sovereign risk and operational failures do not disappear merely because private funding cannot run.

change_log.change: Replaced equity-only loss bearing with designated private risk bearers and qualified the treatment of public support.
change_log.reason: The architecture can permit suitable non-runnable debt, and public guarantees or liquidity support do not necessarily cause realized taxpayer losses.

change_log.change: Retained supported historical dates and the SVB withdrawal amount while describing relevant access and extraction limits.
change_log.reason: The supplied review verifies these specific facts despite partial access to some underlying documents.

change_log.change: Retained Williamson's reported bibliographic details and model conclusion as explicitly unverified research attributions.
change_log.reason: Preserving potentially useful information with uncertainty avoids treating missing evidence as disproof, while respecting the review's finding that no saved text verified it.

change_log.change: Removed the categorical claim that the architecture has not been adopted at system scale.
change_log.reason: Historical proposals and a particular bank failure do not establish worldwide adoption status in November 2026; the freshness search record is empty.

change_log.change: Expanded the proposed demonstration to define backing, system boundaries, stress, payment continuity, credit counterfactuals, information production and reproducibility.
change_log.reason: These additions make the proposed capability testable without presenting candidate thresholds as established standards or finite success as universal proof.

change_log.change: Added explicit overlap and distinctions for every other supplied roster entry.
change_log.reason: Related innovations inform implementation or evaluation but remain separate concepts; roster-only relationships are labeled as synthesis.

change_log.change: Removed the unsupported comparison describing credit-boom forecasting as a lesser, partly achieved task.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence does not establish that achievement ranking.

unresolved_issues: Worldwide adoption and demonstrated performance as of 1 November 2026 remain unknown because the supplied freshness search record is empty.
Diamond and Rajan's exact mechanism, assumptions, publication details and necessity claim require direct verification; the available discussion is secondary.

Williamson's paper identity, July 2024 bibliographic details, reported DOI and welfare result remain unverified from an inspectable artifact. The review's recommendation to omit the reported conclusion entirely was not adopted: it is preserved only as an explicitly unverified attribution, without using it to establish feasibility or impossibility.
The quantitative importance of discipline supplied by fragile funding, and the effectiveness of alternative monitoring and commitment arrangements, remain unresolved.
The proposed demonstration still requires numerical choices for duration, stress severity, acceptable credit contraction and the counterfactual method.
The practical perimeter for runnable substitutes, the exact public backing instrument and transition arrangements remain unspecified.
The supplied evidence does not settle how fiscal or sovereign stress would affect public-backed payment claims, or how costs and benefits would be distributed across users and private risk bearers.

prerequisites.reason: ECO-10 uses run-resistant financing of long-lived loans alongside dependable access to funds as part of its national financial architecture.
